question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund shorted 300 lots of Investment LMN futures (lot size 250) at INR 2,275 on May 16, 9:15 AM. Closing futures price at 4:00 PM on the same day was INR 2,150. What is the MTM P&L?

explanation.text: The Logic: Short profit = (2,275 - 2,150) * 300 * 250 = 125 * 75,000 = INR 93,75,000 profit. Price fell, short position gained. Directly from Example 12.13. The Trap: Loss of INR 93,75,000 reverses direction (longs would lose). INR 3,75,000 forgets lot multiplier or uses only 1 lot. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Equity Derivatives) and XIX-C test MTM calculations. XXI-B tests this for PMS derivative hedges. Manager's Pro-Tip: On daily NAV, always reconcile broker's end-of-day MTM file with internal position - discrepancies of even a few lakh rupees, if unreconciled, will show up as unexplained NAV drift over a quarter and trigger valuer queries.
